items.stem: Two firewall rules conflict: a broad 'allow any' is placed above a specific 'deny'. What happens to the targeted traffic?

options.text: It is allowed, because rules are evaluated top-down and the first match wins
options.rationale: Correct: the first matching rule applies, so the broad allow overrides the later deny.

options.text: It is denied, because deny always wins
options.rationale: Order, not rule type, determines the outcome here.
Rules are still evaluated; the first match applies.

options.text: The firewall crashes on the conflict
options.rationale: A rule-order conflict does not crash the firewall.

items.explanation: Correct: top-down first-match evaluation lets the broad allow win.

items.stem: Which TWO practices support safe firewall management? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Periodically reviewing and removing stale rules
options.rationale: Correct: rule review prevents accumulation of unneeded openings.

options.text: Recording every change with a reason
options.rationale: Correct: change records give an audit trail and aid rollback.

options.text: Keeping an 'allow any any' rule for convenience
options.rationale: A permit-all rule defeats the firewall's purpose.
Disabling logging removes visibility needed to investigate issues.

items.explanation: Correct: rule review and change records both keep a firewall trustworthy.

items.stem: What does stateful inspection add compared with simple packet filtering?

options.text: It tracks connection state so reply traffic is allowed without a separate rule
options.rationale: Correct: stateful firewalls remember established connections.

options.text: It encrypts all traffic by default
options.rationale: Stateful inspection does not provide encryption.

options.text: It removes the need for any rules
options.rationale: Rules are still required to define allowed connections.

options.text: It only works on wireless networks
options.rationale: Stateful inspection is not limited to wireless.

items.explanation: Correct: stateful inspection tracks connection state to permit return traffic.
